topics.summary:
The Zodiac Killer (also known by the pseudonym The Zodiac) is an unidentified serial killer who murdered at least five people in the San Francisco Bay Area between December 1968 and October 1969. The Zodiac attacked three couples and a cab driver in Benicia, Vallejo, unincorporated Napa County, and the city of San Francisco. Two of the Zodiac's seven victims survived.
In a series of letters mailed to Bay Area newspapers, the Zodiac took credit for the murders, described details known only to police, threatened bombings and more murders if the newspapers did not print his letters, and included cryptograms with his correspondence. Two of the Zodiac's four cryptograms were decrypted in 1969 and 2020, and the other two remain unsolved. The Zodiac's last letter was received by the San Francisco Chronicle in 1974. In the letter, the Zodiac claimed to have killed 37 people.
Despite several theories about the Zodiac's true identity, the only suspect police named was Arthur Leigh Allen, a former elementary school teacher and convicted sex offender who died in 1992. topics.summary: On the morning of March 15, 1923, the body of Dorothy King, 29, (born Anna Marie Keenan) was found in her apartment at 144 West 57th Street in the Manhattan borough of New York City, United States. King was a model, actress, and demimondaine whom the press dubbed "The Broadway Butterfly". Her still-unsolved murder was a press sensation at the time it occurred. The term "sugar baby", originally New York City nightlife slang, may have been popularized by journalists reporting on the case.
topics.working_title: The Unsolved Murder of Broadway's 1920s Butterfly
topics.hook: In March 1923, a Manhattan model was found dead in her apartment, triggering a sensational investigation into New York City's high-society nightlife.
topics.why_now: Lesser-known Jazz Age cold cases attract viewers who enjoy vintage mystery and historical noir storytelling.

topics.summary:
The Patomskiy crater or Patom crater (Russian: Патомский кратер, Patomskiy Krater), also known as Конус Колпакова, Konus Kolpakova "Kolpakov cone") is a peculiar rock formation located in the Bodaibo District of the Irkutsk region of southeastern Siberia, 360 kilometres (220 mi) from the district center Bodaibo. It is a large mound made of shattered limestone blocks on the slopes of the Patom Highlands in an area of dense taiga. Its base diameter is about 160 metres (520 ft) and its height about 40 metres (130 ft); the cone's crown is ring-shaped, and in its center there is a smaller mound with a height of about 12 metres (39 ft). The volume of the crater is estimated as 230,000–250,000 cubic metres (8.1–8.8 million cubic feet), with a weight of about one million tons.
The Patomskiy crater was described by Russian geologist Vadim Kolpakov in 1949, though it was known to the local population before this. Its origins have been subject of intense scientific interest, with hypotheses including meteorite, volcanic and gaseous origin, but to date no definite proof has been given. Through dendrochronology, the age of the crater is estimated to be 300 years.
topics.working_title: Siberia's Unexplained Mound: The Mystery of Patomskiy Crater
topics.hook: Deep inside the remote Siberian taiga sits a massive cone of shattered limestone with a strange central mound that challenges conventional geology.
topics.why_now: Visual, remote anomaly cases perform exceptionally well among audiences fascinated by unexplained natural phenomena.

topics.working_title: The Voynich Manuscript: 600 Years and No One Can Read It
topics.hook: A 15th-century book of strange plants, star charts and bathing women, written in a script no codebreaker, linguist or computer has ever read.
topics.why_now: Famous anchor case with over 315,000 Wikipedia views in 60 days and lasting search demand.

topics.working_title: Peter Bergmann: The Man Who Erased Himself in Sligo
topics.hook: In 2009 a man checked into an Irish hotel under a false name and fake Vienna address, spent four days on CCTV quietly getting rid of his belongings, and was found dead on a beach with every label cut from his clothes.
topics.why_now: Lesser-known case with nearly 20,000 views in 60 days, CCTV-driven visuals, and still unidentified.

topics.working_title: The Secret: 12 Buried Treasures, Only 3 Ever Found
topics.hook: In 1982 Byron Preiss buried twelve casques across North America and hid the clues in a book of paintings and riddles; he died in 2005, and most of them are still in the ground.
topics.why_now: Advertiser-friendly puzzle mystery that viewers can still try to solve themselves, with over 16,000 views in 60 days.

topics.working_title: D. B. Cooper: The Man Who Jumped Into the Night (1971)
topics.hook: In 1971 a polite man in a business suit hijacked a Boeing 727 for $200,000, parachuted into a storm over Washington, and was never identified.
topics.why_now: The only unsolved US airline hijacking still pulls 237k Wikipedia views in 60 days, so search demand is huge.

topics.working_title: Room 2805: The Woman Who Erased Herself (Oslo 1995)
topics.hook: A woman checked into Oslo's tallest hotel under a false name and address, and decades later no one knows who she was.
topics.why_now: Lesser-known but rising: steady interest after recent documentaries, and it fits fans of the Peter Bergmann episode.

topics.wiki_title: Lost Library of Ivan the Terrible
topics.working_title: The Lost Library Beneath the Kremlin
topics.hook: A collection of ancient manuscripts said to come from Constantinople vanished in 16th-century Moscow, and people have dug under the Kremlin for it ever since.
topics.why_now: A non-violent historical treasure mystery that broadens the channel and suits a striking thumbnail.

topics.working_title: 536 AD: The Year the Sun Went Dark (And No One Knows Why)
topics.hook: For about 18 months the sun over Constantinople dimmed, summers froze and harvests failed across the Northern Hemisphere, and scientists still can't agree which volcano caused it.
topics.why_now: Hugely searched 'worst year to be alive' story (41k Wikipedia views in 60 days) with an open scientific whodunit at its heart.

topics.working_title: The Carroll A. Deering: A Ghost Ship With No Crew (1921)
topics.hook: In January 1921 a five-masted schooner ran aground off Cape Hatteras with its sails set and food in the galley, and its entire crew was never seen again.
topics.why_now: Classic ghost-ship mystery that rides the same interest as the Flying Dutchman, but with real people, real records and a federal investigation.

topics.working_title: The Bennington Triangle: 5 People Vanished in Vermont's Woods
topics.hook: Between 1945 and 1950 several people walked into the woods around Glastenbury Mountain, Vermont, and never came out, including college student Paula Jean Welden on a December afternoon hike.
topics.why_now: Lesser-known 'triangle' with strong search interest in Paula Welden, perfect for an eerie, atmospheric autumn-into-winter video.
